newsitem.title: UK: Britain's SFO seeks Nadir arrest in Turkey - report.
newsitem.headline: Britain's SFO seeks Nadir arrest in Turkey - report.

text.p: Britain's Serious Fraud Office has sent officers to Turkey to seek the arrest of fugitive Turkish Cypriot tycoon Asil Nadir four years after he jumped bail in the UK, the Times reported on Friday.

The newspaper said the SFO had sent the officers to Turkey to talk to judicial authorities there. The Turkish police are members of Interpol, which has been alerted by the SFO to be on the lookout for Nadir.
Nadir told Reuters on Thursday he was heading for Turkey from his home in northern Cyprus.
His solicitor Peter Krivinskas told the Times that Nadir had some work to do in Turkey.
Nadir fled Britain in May 1993 while awaiting trial on theft and false accounting charges following the collapse of his London-based Polly Peck fruits to electronics empire.
He still has media, banking and tourism interests in breakaway northern Cyprus.
Krivinskas said he did not believe the Turkish courts would allow Nadir, a Turkish citizen, to be extradited in these circumstances.
Nadir cannot be extradited from northern Cyprus, where he has just launched a radio station, as the country is not recognised by the UK.
Turkey invaded northern Cyrpus in 1974 after a short-lived military coup on the island. Only Ankara recognises Northern Cyprus.
